keyVerseText: Seven years old was Jehoash when he began to reign.
rootMeaning: The name יְהוֹאָשׁ (Yᵉhôwʼâsh) combines the divine name יְהֹוָה (Yᵉhôvâh), meaning 'the existing One' or Jehovah, with a second element possibly related to fire (אֵשׁ), suggesting a meaning along the lines of 'Jehovah-fired' or 'given by the Lord.' This etymology highlights a personal connection to God as the source of life and power, beyond the simple transliteration 'Jehoash.' It emphasizes divine empowerment or a gift bestowed by God, enriching the understanding of the name beyond a mere label to a theological statement about God's active role in the king's identity.
usageInScripture: The word יְהוֹאָשׁ appears 17 times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently translated as 'Jehoash' or with slight variations such as 'And Jehoash' or 'of Jehoash.' This reflects its primary use as a proper name for two kings—one of Judah and one of Israel. The consistent use of the name in historical and narrative contexts underscores its role as an identifier tied to royal lineage and divine appointment. The variations in translation do not alter the core recognition of Jehoash as a divinely given name, affirming the biblical authors’ emphasis on the king’s relationship to God.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יְהוֹאָשׁ as 'given by the Lord' or 'Jehovah-fired' deepens our appreciation of biblical kingship as not merely political but divinely ordained. It reminds believers that God is sovereign over history and leadership, actively bestowing authority and purpose. This name points to the reality that God’s presence and power are integral to the legitimacy and mission of His anointed servants. For the Christian faith, it foreshadows the ultimate King, Jesus Christ, whose authority is fully rooted in God’s divine will and empowerment. The name Jehoash thus invites reflection on God's providence and the calling of leaders to serve under His guidance.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Kings 11:21, 'Seven years old was Jehoash when he began to reign,' the name Jehoash highlights that even from a young age, this king’s authority is recognized as given by God. The word יְהוֹאָשׁ in this verse anchors the young king’s reign in divine appointment, signaling that God’s hand is upon him despite his youth. This encourages believers to trust in God's sovereign timing and empowerment, knowing that leadership and service begin under God's provision and purpose.
